explanations.why: Part3.pdf specifically names the SG UNIT-2 FLR WASH WTR TRANSFER PUMPS as 2W, which is corroborated by Part4.pdf p.58, whereas Part1.pdf p.43 refers to WASTE WATER TRANSFER PUMPS.
explanations.consequence: If the wrong value is used, the pumps could lack standby redundancy or fail to handle the full required flow, leading to floor wash water flooding during pump failures or peak loads.

explanations.why: Part3.pdf specifically identifies the floor wash water transfer pumps as having 2 working units, corroborated by Part4.pdf p.58, while Part1.pdf p.43 describes waste water transfer pumps.
explanations.consequence: If only 1 working pump is provided when 2 are needed for normal capacity, the system will have insufficient pumping capacity and floor wash water will back up in the unit.
